analysis.method: Envelope of complete-data Paired Bounds over every binary completion; exact outward binomial bounds
assumptions: Latent complete case vectors are independent identically distributed draws from the target population.
Retain the fixed planned case set and full candidate family, including wholly missing rows and columns.
Observed 0/1 outcomes are correct; ? means unknown, never an observed pass or fail.
No missing-at-random assumption is needed: every binary completion is enclosed, even outcome-dependent masking.
Fix final sample size, pass rule, family, alpha and margin before observing outcomes; no repeated looks or optional stopping.
Unlisted or selectively omitted cases, correlated cases, selected families and incorrect observed labels invalidate coverage.
Sample identification bounds describe possible completed sample means, not population confidence bounds.
Non-establishment of a criterion is inconclusive; pins establish byte identity, not honesty or prospective choices.

display.rounding_error_means: display minus exact, in percentage points

limits: Original rational intervals and decisions are retained unchanged; displayed intervals are enlarged outward.
Coverage requires latent complete case vectors to be independent identically distributed draws, with fixed planned rows and full candidate family.
Every planned row is retained; ? is unknown, never imputed as pass or failure. Unlisted cases cannot be detected.
Sample identification intervals describe possible completed sample means, not population confidence bounds.
No missing-at-random assumption is needed; every binary completion is enclosed. This does not repair selective omission, optional stopping or inaccurate observations.
Coverage is repeated-sampling, not a posterior probability; rounding adds no measurement evidence.
The practical margin is an absolute rate difference: 0.1 means ten percentage points, not a relative percent improvement.
Displayed comparisons use the exact unrounded margin and may be inconclusive when the original criterion passes.
A false criterion does not establish its opposite; do not choose precision, margin or family after inspecting outcomes.
Input pins prove byte identity, not honest execution, representative sampling or prospective choices.
